Final categorization: OK

Justification: This original research paper focuses centrally on predicting and mapping land use change (LUC) dynamics in Brazil, a national-scale explicit spatial implementation. It develops and applies an integrated spatially explicit modeling framework combining a global CGE model (MAGNET), a spatial land use allocation model (PLUC), and a GIS-based carbon module to simulate future LUC patterns in Brazil toward 2030 under multiple scenarios. The study implements more than one scenario, including a reference and several mitigation measure scenarios, with quantitative comparisons of resulting land use changes and associated greenhouse gas emissions. The outputs include mapped spatial projections of LUC at a 25 km² resolution for the entire country, with quantitative assessment of area changes and emissions. The paper meets all core inclusion criteria: national-scale spatial modeling, primary focus on LUC prediction, multiple future scenarios, spatially explicit quantitative modeling, and mapped LUC outputs. It does not meet any exclusion criteria. Although bioenergy and emissions are discussed, the central research question and modeling effort revolve around LUC prediction and mitigation at the national scale. Therefore, the paper is categorized as OK.
